newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ job ads down 2.3 percent in September - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ job ads down 2.3 percent in September - ANZ.

text.p: The trend number of job ads fell 2.3 percent in September and 8.7 percent in the year to September, ANZ Bank said on Tuesday.
ANZ said job ads have declined for five consecutive months in the three main centres, with Wellington displaying the largest decrease in job advertisement numbers in annual terms.
"Nevertheless, the number of advertised jobs remains at higher levels in all of the three main centres than during 1991 and 1992," it said.

Job ads in Wellington fell 2.2 percent in September and were down 20.2 percent on an annual basis. In Auckland ads fell 2.2 percent in September, following a 2.3 percent fall in August. They were 6.6 percent lower than in September 1995.
Jobs ads in Christchurch fell 2.8 percent in September and 9.6 percent in the year.
The amount of job advertising is regarded as a leading indicator of economic activity.
"The recent fall in job ads is consistent with the weakening in economic activity which has occurred over the course of the past 12 months," ANZ said.
Production-based GDP fell to 2.6 percent in the June 1996 year from 4.8 percent in the June 1995 year.
"Our forecasts indicate that GDP growth will reach a trough in the latter half of 1996," ANZ said.
